# Staged release queue for .github/workflows/release.yml
#
# One "<version> <full-40-char-commit-sha>" per line, oldest first. The
# scheduled job releases the FIRST entry that is not on npm yet, so the queue
# advances itself and never needs writing back to. Keyed on the registry rather
# than on tags, because a version can be tagged and released on GitHub while its
# npm publish is still pending — a tag-based check would skip it forever.
#
# The SHA must be the full 40 characters. An abbreviation can become ambiguous
# as the repo grows, and a branch or tag name is mutable, so "release the queued
# commit" would quietly mean "release whatever that ref points at this morning".
# scripts/verify-release.sh and the workflow both refuse anything else.
#
# 0.4.0-0.17.0 were staged here and are NOT released. They were development
# milestones with release notes, authored across three days, never independently
# validated and never installed by anyone. Publishing them in sequence would
# have left npm's `latest` on 0.3.0 — which drops the DDS event backlog on
# subscribe, the exact failure this tool exists to catch — for another month,
# and would have put 0.17.0's since-retracted Bloc claim on `latest` en route.
# Their history stays in CHANGELOG.md, which is where it belongs.
#
# To pause releases: comment out the remaining lines, or disable the workflow.
# To reorder or skip: edit this file. Nothing else reads it.

0.18.0  af8ed0947414a87c6089b5a8aec5cbd61c39ff7f
